nws.title: Weather Service watches and warnings
nws.detail: Nothing for Western New York right now.

ao.title: Arctic Oscillation: is cold air escaping?
ao.detail: Model average goes as low as -1.3 (Nov 4) and as high as +1.3. Below -2 = cold air can escape south. Above +2.5 = cold stays up north.

nao.title: North Atlantic Oscillation: is cold air steered our way?
nao.detail: Model average goes as low as -0.4 (Nov 11) and as high as +1.0. Below -1.5 = cold air gets steered into the East.

cpc610.title: NOAA 6–10 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc610.detail: Nov 2–Nov 6: 60% chance of being warmer than normal.

cpc814.title: NOAA 8–14 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc814.detail: Nov 4–Nov 10: 40% chance of being warmer than normal.

erie.title: Lake Erie water temperature
erie.detail: Oct 26: 4°F warmer than normal (58°F). Record for the date: 62.1°F (2017). Warmer water = more fuel for lake-effect snow.

vortex.title: Will the polar vortex break down?
vortex.detail: In 20 of 31 runs of the American weather model, the spinning winds over the Arctic stop and reverse within 30 days, as early as Nov 4. That can send Arctic air south 1 to 3 weeks later. Yesterday: 35%.

noreaster.title: Nor'easter in the next 10 days?
noreaster.detail: No model runs show a strong storm off the Northeast coast. Strongest run: 992 mb (lower = stronger).

freeze.title: First freeze in Buffalo
freeze.detail: Not yet this fall. 2 of 31 model runs freeze within 10 days, around Nov 6. Coldest run: 27°F.

arctic.title: Arctic air over Buffalo?
arctic.detail: 0 of 31 model runs bring air colder than 14°F about 5,000 ft up in the next 10 days. Coldest run: 16°F up there.

lakeeffect.title: Lake-effect snow setup?
lakeeffect.detail: 3 of 31 model runs get cold enough over Lake Erie (62°F water) for lake-effect snow around Nov 6. 84% show lake-effect rain showers.

recent.text: 🌊 Lake Erie is unusually warm for Oct 26: 61.9°F, about 4°F warmer than normal. The record for this date is 62.1°F (2017). Warm lake water is fuel for lake-effect snow: when cold air blows over it, the lake adds heat and moisture, which can build heavier snow bands.

🌪️ The polar vortex may break down. The polar vortex is a huge spinning wind high above the Arctic that usually keeps the coldest air locked up north. In 20 of 31 runs of the American weather model (65%), that spin stops and reverses, as early as Nov 4. When that happens, Arctic air often spills south 1 to 3 weeks later, which can mean cold and snow for Buffalo. Yesterday it was 35%.
